subject.title: [Bug]: Performance degradation in session memory sync: full delete-reinsert pattern for growing JSONL files

question: Should this issue be fixed as a fresh current-main incremental session indexing implementation, rescued from the conflicting open PR, or intentionally left as full-entry reindex behavior?
rationale: The choice affects session-state correctness, schema behavior, batching semantics, and whether the old candidate branch is worth adopting.

options.title: Fresh current-main fix
options.body: Implement incremental session indexing against the current `memory_index_*` schema and source-wide batching paths with focused upgrade and compaction coverage.

options.title: Rescue the open PR
options.body: Ask the contributor or a maintainer to rebase https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75179 and replace obsolete assumptions before further review.

options.title: Keep full reindex
options.body: Leave the existing full-entry behavior if maintainers decide consistency is worth the extra long-session indexing cost.

recommendation.title: Fresh current-main fix
recommendation.body: Implement incremental session indexing against the current `memory_index_*` schema and source-wide batching paths with focused upgrade and compaction coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent storage/schema history makes this the best available owner for the schema-sensitive design choice.
